title: jokes4
summary: A long collection of light-bulb jokes, the familiar "How many does it take to change a light bulb?" format, gathered from various sources and circulated widely in print and online. Each entry is a short one-line or few-line gag that targets a group, profession, nationality, or stereotype: lawyers, philosophy majors, programmers, Mac users, bureaucrats, Harvard students, Texans-style regional rivals such as Oregonians and Californians, New Yorkers, Iranians, Russians, feminists, yuppies, and psychiatrists. Some entries are attributed to sources such as a 1985 Boston Ad Club calendar and a Wall Street Journal item from October 1985, and others are riffs on surrealism, Zen, or Carl Sagan. The humor relies on punchlines that play on literalness, absurd escalation, and self-deprecation. The file contains no single author or narrative, and the entries are anonymous folk material. It is a light, topical, and occasionally dated compilation, with a few entries that rely on period references to politicians and corporations.
